description: Discriminator: in an environment where the fixed probe address cannot be dialled, does the local-address helper return an address or panic? Prefix: the harness calls the helper itself and wraps only that call in recover, so the observation is reported instead of killing the test. Controls: the result prints whether it panicked, the panic value and whether any value was produced; the same call is the one replica construction makes inline.

harness.description: In-package Go test that calls the implementation's local-address helper and reports whether it returns or panics.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: no replica is constructed; the helper is called directly
the call is wrapped in recover() to observe a panic; the replica constructor has no recover around it

legality.derivation: The helper is a package-level function with no inputs, so calling it directly exercises exactly what the constructor evaluates.
legality.applicability: The execution environment cannot dial the probe address.
unresolved: no prerequisite event exists because the helper takes no input; the panic value is the observation

grounding.derivation: The event reports whether the helper returned or panicked, which is the duty's observable.

observable_properties.description: Resolving the local address must not panic when the probe address is unreachable.

uncertainties: the check observes the helper rather than a full replica construction, because construction also needs peer addresses and a listener
whether the project's own deployments always reach the probe address
